When you can state the edit you believe is correct and the\r\nedit that must break with the stage it breaks at, the question is a claim for the `prove` tool the\r\n`probe` MCP server registers, and `.claude/rules/quality.md` § Instruments owns that rule. When the\r\nquestion carries no stated belief to falsify yet, when the subject lies outside the TypeScript a\r\nworkspace project judges, or when the proof needs what that tool's stages do not model — a process\r\ntree, a listening socket, an installed package, a built entry driven as a child, or a live external\r\nservice — write a probe.\r\n\r\nThe kinds split by which tool has to see the probe:\r\n\r\n- A **type probe** is read by `tsc`, whose scoped project includes only its own environment, so it\r\n  lives in the source tree beside what it measures. Delete it before the unit returns; a leaked one\r\n  fails the `policy` plugin's placement rules, because a probe filename is not a centralized kind\r\n  file.\r\n- A **runtime probe** is collected by a Vitest project, so it lives in `tmp/probe/` and runs through\r\n  the `probe` project. `tmp/` is ignored by git, so no probe enters a commit by accident, and every\r\n  test script names its project, so no gate runs the `probe` project.\r\n- A **bench** is read by Vitest's benchmark mode, so it lives inside a test file as a block behind\r\n  the `if (import.meta.env.MODE === 'benchmark')` guard. Only the `test:bench` script collects the\r\n  block, test mode fails an unguarded `bench()` call loudly, and no gate runs a bench. Call `bench`\r\n  directly inside the guard. A `describe` inside it trips `vitest/no-conditional-tests`, and a suite\r\n  the guard leaves unregistered fails test mode with `No test found in suite`.\r\n\r\nRun a probe before relying on an unverified belief about behaviour: what a function returns, what a\r\nconfiguration resolves to, whether a path is reached at all. Prefer a probe to an argument whenever\r\nthe probe is cheap.\r\n\r\nWhen the question is whether the difference between methods is a magnitude or negligible, write a\r\nguarded bench block beside the probe test and run the `test:bench` script. Declare the threshold\r\nbefore the run, read the ratio between the methods against each side's reported uncertainty, and\r\nrecord nothing below a magnitude. A settled magnitude that underwrites an implementation choice\r\npromotes with its test into the mirrored suite and keeps its guarded block there while that choice\r\nstands. A deterministic relationship promotes as an ordinary assertion, so delete the block. Never\r\ncommit baseline output.\r\n\r\nThese rules bind every probe:\r\n\r\n- **Prove the instrument can fail before trusting that it passed.** Pair it with a control drawn\r\n  from outside the population it covers.\r\n- **Promote or delete.** A probe that settles a claim becomes a test in the mirrored location that\r\n  proves the real source. Delete every other probe. A probe left in the suite reports on the harness\r\n  while reading as a test.\r\n- **Never commit a probe.** The ignore rule stops an accident, not a deliberate forced add, and a\r\n  type probe sits in tracked source with no ignore rule at all.\r\n\r\n## Live-service tests\r\n\r\nLive external services/models are the deliberate exception to fast hermetic defaults:\r\n\r\n- Put them in the `service` project, under `tests/service/`, with `tests/setupService.ts` for setup\r\n  and a longer timeout. That module's presence is what registers the project, so a live proof with\r\n  no readiness setup is a project nothing configures.\r\n- `.claude/rules/workspace.md` fixes which gate runs the `service` project, and that gate is not the\r\n  same one in a publishing and a `private: true` workspace.\r\n- Warm and verify service readiness in `tests/setupService.ts`.\r\n- Hard-require readiness: throw loudly; never silently skip.\r\n- Verify service-dependent logic through that service's project, not unrelated module tests or scattered conditional skips.\r\n- Tune each request to the smallest input/context/output that proves one behavior without becoming brittle or expensive.\r\n- Prefer semantic bounded assertions over exact generated prose. Increase context/workload only when the scenario requires it.\r\n\r\n## Expensive proofs\r\n\r\nA test that spawns a process, packs, installs, or drives a real build is a proof, not a unit test.\r\n\r\n- Give it its own Vitest project with its own setup and timeout.\r\n- Keep it out of the default run where the workspace has a gate that can hold it.\r\n  `.claude/rules/workspace.md` fixes which gate each isolated project runs from, and that placement\r\n  differs between a publishing and a `private: true` workspace.\r\n- The fixed expensive-proof projects are `distribution` and `service`.\r\n- A `distribution` proof reads `import.meta.env.MODE` and fails, rather than skips, on an unreachable\r\n  registry under `--mode release`. The publish gate invokes it that way, so a proof that skips there\r\n  passes the gate without ever proving the artifact installs. An ordinary local run may still skip.\r\n- Slow and hermetic is reason enough to isolate a proof; it need not touch an external service.\r\n- Where such a proof stays in a shared project, size its budget from a full contended run rather than from an isolated one. A budget that clears the isolated cost by a thin margin turns contention into a red gate reporting a timeout, which carries no diagnostic about the code and costs a full investigation to dismiss.\r\n\r\n## Shared test infrastructure\r\n\r\nTest helpers are shared infrastructure, not local test-file clutter.\r\n\r\n`@orkestrel/test` owns the helpers every workspace repeats: the call recorder, the real delay, the JSON and async collectors, and the owned scratch directory. Import them from `@orkestrel/test`, and its Node-only helpers from `@orkestrel/test/server`. Write a helper of your own only where the package exports none for the job. The following shapes are the contract a workspace codes against, not source to copy.\r\n\r\n- For the vendored test set (`tests/setupPolicy.ts`, `tests/policy.test.ts`, and\r\n  `tests/config.test.ts`), keep shared helpers within that set instead of importing them from\r\n  `@orkestrel/test`; follow the vendored-file import law in `.claude/rules/workspace.md`.\r\n\r\n- Extract a fixture, recorder, event factory, async wait, renderer, scenario/data builder, protocol fixture, or DOM builder as soon as it could serve another test.\r\n- Any duplicate or near-duplicate helper is a defect; consolidate it into one general form.\r\n- Export every reusable helper, fixture type, factory, constant, and guard from setup files.\r\n- A setup file owns everything an assertion needs and nothing an assertion is: `describe`, `it`, and `expect` never appear in a `setup*.ts`.\r\n- Data tables and case matrices belong in a setup file at any size; test registration does not.\r\n- Test files import shared infrastructure rather than declaring local fixture factories.\r\n- Never reimplement a framework helper in tests or fixtures; import the real parser, signer, flattener, or other helper.\r\n- Prefer small customizable factories/stubs that seed inert data for a real scenario over repeated inline setup.\r\n- Helper names follow module-helper naming: `createFixtureServer`, `buildElement`, `appendItems`, `renderRows`, `waitForReady`, `extractDetail`.\r\n\r\nPlace helpers by environment:\r\n\r\n- `tests/setup.ts`: host-independent; no `node:*`, DOM, `window`, or Vue.\r\n- `tests/setupServer.ts`: Node-only helpers and `node:fs` loaders anchored to `WORKSPACE_ROOT`.\r\n- `tests/setupBrowser.ts`: DOM/Vue/browser helpers and setup CSS.\r\n- `tests/setupStyles.ts`: CSS/style helpers and compiled cascade.\r\n\r\n### Recorder\r\n\r\nImport `createRecorder` from `@orkestrel/test` instead of a framework spy when only calls and arguments matter. It returns:\r\n\r\n```ts\r\ninterface RecorderInterface<TArgs extends readonly unknown[]> {\r\n\treadonly calls: readonly TArgs[]\r\n\treadonly count: number\r\n\treadonly handler: (...args: TArgs) => void\r\n\tclear(): void\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\n### Delay\r\n\r\nImport `waitForDelay` from `@orkestrel/test`; never repeat an inline timeout promise. It waits for one host timer and defaults to `0`:\r\n\r\n```ts\r\nfunction waitForDelay(ms?: number): Promise<void>\r\n```\r\n\r\nUse it to yield, never to wait for something another process produces. A fixed delay chosen to\r\noutlast a child's startup is a race whose loss looks like a product defect: the test measures\r\ninterpreter bootstrap rather than the behaviour it names, and it fails on a loaded host and passes on\r\nan idle one. Wait until a named condition holds instead, polling with `waitForDelay` inside a budget\r\nmeasured by `performance.now()`, and fail with the condition's own description when the budget\r\nexpires.\r\n\r\n### Scratch\r\n\r\nImport `createScratch` from `@orkestrel/test/server` when a proof needs real files. It allocates a temporary directory it owns, contains every path against escape, and removes the directory on `destroy`:\r\n\r\n```ts\r\ninterface ScratchInterface {\r\n\treadonly path: string\r\n\twrite(target: string, text: string): string\r\n\tread(target: string): string | undefined\r\n\thas(target: string): boolean\r\n\tnames(target?: string): readonly string[]\r\n\tensure(target: string): string\r\n\tlink(target: string, source: string): string\r\n\tremove(target: string): void\r\n\tdestroy(): void\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\n### Style primitives\r\n\r\nBrowser/style setup exposes shared assertions/builders:\r\n\r\n`mount`, `render`, `build`, `readStyle`, `readToken`, `readRootToken`, `readPixels`, `parseCSSColor`, `matchesColor`, `findRule`.\r\n\r\n`findRule` proves a declaration exists in the cascade; `readStyle()` reads the resolved result.\r\n\r\n## Browser tests\r\n\r\nUse the real browser as the system under test:\r\n\r\n- Do not replace DOM events, storage, observers, viewports, layout methods, pointer, or drag APIs unless the browser genuinely lacks one.\r\n- Prefer real nodes, events, styles/layout, and observers.\r\n- Centralize event factories: `createPointerEvent`, `createDragEvent`, `typeInput`, `fireTransitionEnd`.\r\n- Centralize DOM builders: `createButtonElement`, `createDropdownElements`, `createModalElement`.\r\n- Assert DOM state, emitted events, callback records, focus, classes, attributes, and public API state.\r\n- Do not assert private state, internal timers, or framework scheduler internals.\r\n- Prefer real short timers and observable wakeups. Never replace the host clock.\r\n\r\n## Runner configuration\r\n\r\nKeep Vitest/provider configuration minimal:\r\n\r\n- Prefer defaults until a measured problem proves them insufficient.\r\n- Centralize provider setup in one helper/shared block.\r\n- Add browser/provider/teardown/timeout/parallelism/cache/launch settings only for a current verified need.\r\n- Avoid long browser flag lists and persistent contexts unless a test requires them.\r\n- For slow teardown, inspect test cleanup, open handles, file parallelism, and context churn before adding launch flags.\r\n- Remove exploratory settings after fixing the cause.\r\n- Config comments explain the current reason, not the history of failed experiments.\r\n\r\n## Untestable usually means missing seam\r\n\r\nBefore accepting that a behavior cannot be tested, look for the seam that would make it testable.\r\n\r\n- Treat a collaborator reached through a hard-coded global — a stream, a clock source, a spawn, a fetch — as a missing injection point, not an untestable truth.\r\n- An injected collaborator with a real minimal implementation is a sanctioned boundary stub, not a mock of project-owned behavior.\r\n- Add the seam rather than shipping the gap whenever the design would welcome it anyway, and whenever a sibling collaborator is already injected.\r\n- Record a genuinely irreducible gap where a reader meets it: what is unproven, why it cannot be driven, and what would change that. A silent untested guard reads exactly like a tested one.\r\n\r\nCoverage rules:\r\n\r\n- Read a coverage report as a discovery input, never as evidence of proof. It answers one cheap mechanical question — which code no test executed — and that reliably finds forgotten branches and rules nothing calls.\r\n- Never cite coverage as the adequacy audit's result. It cannot tell you whether an executed line is asserted, so a fully covered file can still be entirely unproven.\r\n- Never let a percentage become the target.\r\n\r\n## Discovery and adequacy audit\r\n\r\nBefore acceptance:\r\n\r\n- prove every intended test file is discovered by the correct project;\r\n- prove every declared project is reachable from a gate. A project registered in the root\r\n  configuration with no script, or with a script no chain runs, is a proof that never executes — and\r\n  because it never executes it never fails, so the suite reports green while carrying it. Read the\r\n  chain, not the exit code: run each project directly once and compare that list against what `test`\r\n  actually invokes. The gate that would report this gap is the gate that is missing.\r\n- prove a declared project's include resolves to a real file. An empty project is not a passing\r\n  project: Vitest exits non-zero on \"no test files found\", so a project aimed at a path that was\r\n  never created stays invisible until something finally runs it.\r\n- inspect actual test counts and environments;\r\n- audit `.todo`, `.skip`, conditional skips, retries, and inflated timeouts;\r\n- confirm each assertion would fail for the defect it claims to catch, and that it fails rather than passes when its population is empty;\r\n- confirm helpers do not reimplement production behavior;\r\n- confirm cleanup runs after setup or assertion failure;\r\n- confirm current-scope requirements have real tests rather than placeholders.\r\n---\r\npaths:\r\n  - 'src/**/*'\r\n  - 'app/**/*'\r\n  - 'tests/**/*'\r\n  - 'configs/**/*'\r\n  - 'demo/**/*'\r\n  - 'package.json'\r\n  - 'tsconfig.json'\r\n  - 'vite.config.ts'\r\n---\r\n\r\n# Workspace, environments, builds, and scripts\r\n\r\nUse only the environments a project needs, and keep the root dependency model intact while doing it.\r\n\r\n## Environments\r\n\r\n| Path           | Purpose                                                       |\r\n| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |\r\n| `src/core/`    | Published host-independent library                            |\r\n| `src/browser/` | Published browser-only library                                |\r\n| `src/server/`  | Published Node-only library                                   |\r\n| `src/styles/`  | Optional SCSS bundle producing `index.css`                    |\r\n| `src/bin/`     | Optional executable; `main.ts` entry, never a public barrel   |\r\n| `app/core/`    | Shared application logic with an `index.ts` barrel            |\r\n| `app/browser/` | Browser app; `main.ts` entry, not a barrel                    |\r\n| `app/server/`  | Node server app; `main.ts` entry                              |\r\n| `tests/`       | Mirrors src/app environments; root holds cross-cutting proofs |\r\n| `configs/`     | Thin target wrappers around root configs                      |\r\n\r\n- Dependency direction is the root project model in `AGENTS.md` and is not restated here; this file governs where the environments live and how they are configured.\r\n- Typical browser-app domains: `components/`, `pages/`, `composables/`, `controllers/`, `services/`, `stores/`.\r\n- Typical server-app domains: `handlers.ts`, `middlewares.ts`, `routes.ts`.\r\n- `src/styles/index.ts` is a side-effect entry importing `./index.scss`.\r\n- `src/bin/main.ts` is the executable entry, built to `dist/bin/main.js`. The name is fixed, as it\r\n  is for `app/browser/main.ts` and `app/server/main.ts`, so every runtime entry in a workspace is\r\n  found at the same name.\r\n- `package.json`'s `bin` key is the installed command name. The entry path is the value and does\r\n  not carry that name.\r\n\r\n## Aliases\r\n\r\n| Alias          | Target                 |\r\n| -------------- | ---------------------- |\r\n| `@src/core`    | `src/core/index.ts`    |\r\n| `@src/browser` | `src/browser/index.ts` |\r\n| `@src/server`  | `src/server/index.ts`  |\r\n| `@src/styles`  | `src/styles/index.ts`  |\r\n| `@app/core`    | `app/core/index.ts`    |\r\n| `@app/browser` | `app/browser/index.ts` |\r\n| `@app/server`  | `app/server/index.ts`  |\r\n\r\nDefine aliases in `tsconfig.json` first. `vite.config.ts` derives from `compilerOptions.paths`; keep both aligned.\r\n\r\n## Configuration authority\r\n\r\n- `tsconfig.json`: shared compiler options, all-tree types, and path aliases.\r\n- `vite.config.ts`: shared builds, test projects, environment loading/mapping, and aliases.\r\n- `*/types.ts`: public API contracts.\r\n- `configs/src/` and `configs/app/`: thin per-target wrappers, including optional\r\n  `configs/src/*bin*` files. Shared logic remains in root configs.\r\n- `configs/helpers.ts`, `configs/browsers.ts`, and `configs/policy.ts`: the only permitted leaves\r\n  under `configs/`. Each imports nothing from the workspace, which is what keeps it a leaf, so no\r\n  `configs/types.ts` exists for one to import: each keeps its own types, data, and functions in its\r\n  one file, and the centralized-kind placement in `.claude/rules/architecture.md` does not reach a\r\n  leaf. Each `configs/src/*.config.ts` imports the root config rather than a leaf, so shared build\r\n  logic stays in one place.\r\n- Keep `configs/helpers.ts` free of any dependency a core-only workspace does not declare. It is\r\n  vendored byte-identical to every workspace, so an import there must resolve in all of them.\r\n  `configs/browsers.ts` exists for that reason: it imports `playwright` and\r\n  `@vitest/browser-playwright`, and only a workspace with a browser environment is given it.\r\n- Keep `configs/policy.ts` free of imports entirely. It is the workspace's oxlint plugin, the lint\r\n  instrument of the policy law, and it is vendored byte-identical to every workspace including a\r\n  core-only one, so a module that imports nothing at all is the only form that resolves in all of\r\n  them.\r\n- When a file is vendored byte-identical, import only what resolves in every workspace: a `node:`\r\n  module, or a package `BASE_DEV_DEPENDENCIES` declares. Refuse any other `@orkestrel/*` import;\r\n  `tests/src/server/helpers.test.ts` reads every vendored JavaScript and TypeScript module against\r\n  that set. A base package resolves in its own checkout through its `exports` map to its built\r\n  `dist/` entry, so a vendored module that imports it runs there after `npm run build`; the\r\n  generated root `tsconfig.json` maps the workspace's own published specifiers to its source, so\r\n  `npm run check` there needs no build.\r\n\r\nEnvironment rules:\r\n\r\n- `vite.config.ts` owns environment loading/mapping.\r\n- Add shared variables there first.\r\n- Prefer a minimal plain set such as `APP_NAME`, `APP_API_PATH`, `APP_HOST`, `APP_PORT`.\r\n- Expose extra browser runtime values only for a concrete need.\r\n\r\n## Build outputs\r\n\r\n| Output             | Content                        | Format          |\r\n| ------------------ | ------------------------------ | --------------- |\r\n| `dist/src/core`    | Core library + declarations    | ES and CJS      |\r\n| `dist/src/browser` | Browser library + declarations | ES              |\r\n| `dist/src/server`  | Server library + declarations  | ES and CJS      |\r\n| `dist/src/styles`  | Compiled `index.css`           | ES wrapper      |\r\n| `dist/bin`         | Optional executable `main.js`  | ES with shebang |\r\n| `dist/app/browser` | Browser application            | target-defined  |\r\n| `dist/app/server`  | Server application             | CJS             |\r\n| `dist/showcase`    | Single-file `index.html` demo  | self-contained  |\r\n\r\n- Library declarations are emitted by `tsc` through `configs/src/tsconfig.{core,browser,server}.json`, chained after each Vite build.\r\n- Styles ship CSS, not declarations.\r\n- Optional `appShowcase` uses `configs/app/vite.showcase.config.ts` and `vite-plugin-singlefile` to create a minified file-URL-safe `dist/showcase/index.html`.\r\n- The showcase is outside the default build.\r\n- Use Oxc for showcase JS minification and Lightning CSS for CSS.\r\n- Inject a `build-id` meta stamp so rebuilt `file://` demos cache-bust.\r\n\r\n## Test project matrix\r\n\r\n`vite.config.ts` defines Vitest projects on an environment axis and a workspace-proof axis. The\r\nenvironment axis is one project per src/app axis × environment:\r\n\r\n| Project       | Files                  | Environment         | Setup                                           |\r\n| ------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |\r\n| `src:core`    | `tests/src/core/**`    | Node                | `setup.ts`                                      |\r\n| `src:browser` | `tests/src/browser/**` | Playwright Chromium | `setup.ts`, `setupBrowser.ts`                   |\r\n| `src:server`  | `tests/src/server/**`  | Node                | `setup.ts`, `setupServer.ts`                    |\r\n| `src:styles`  | `tests/src/styles/**`  | Playwright Chromium | `setup.ts`, `setupBrowser.ts`, `setupStyles.ts` |\r\n| `src:bin`     | `tests/src/bin/**`     | Node                | `setup.ts`, `setupServer.ts`                    |\r\n| `app:core`    | `tests/app/core/**`    | Node                | `setup.ts`                                      |\r\n| `app:browser` | `tests/app/browser/**` | Playwright Chromium | `setup.ts`, `setupBrowser.ts`                   |\r\n| `app:server`  | `tests/app/server/**`  | Node                | `setup.ts`, `setupServer.ts`                    |\r\n\r\nThe workspace-proof axis is cross-cutting. Each proof covers the whole workspace rather than\r\none environment, so each is its own project:\r\n\r\n| Project        | Files                        | Proves                                                                                                                                                                                       | Gate                                  |\r\n| -------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |\r\n| `policy`       | `tests/policy.test.ts`       | The path- and text-shaped policy laws: mirrors, suppressions, the rule map, filenames, manifest scripts, skills, and bridges                                                                 | `test`                                |\r\n| `config`       | `tests/config.test.ts`       | Root configuration resolves its aliases, projects, and outputs                                                                                                                               | `test`                                |\r\n| `setup`        | `tests/setup*.test.ts`       | Reusable behavior exported from the root test setup modules works as the consuming suites require                                                                                            | `test`                                |\r\n| `guides`       | `tests/guides.test.ts`       | Every documented API exists, every public API is documented, every compared summary, example, and pitch equals its source, and every executable fence returns what the guide says it returns | `test`                                |\r\n| `conformance`  | `tests/conformance.test.ts`  | Where this package drifts from the official tooling it tracks                                                                                                                                | `test`                                |\r\n| `distribution` | `tests/distribution.test.ts` | The packed package installs and resolves through its public exports                                                                                                                          | `prepublishOnly`; absent when private |\r\n| `integration`  | `tests/integration.test.ts`  | The package's features work together end to end across environments                                                                                                                          | `test`                                |\r\n| `service`      | `tests/service/**/*.test.ts` | The live external services this package drives, driven for real                                                                                                                              | `prepublishOnly`; `test` when private |\r\n\r\n- Define the `setup` project only when a root file matches `tests/setup*.test.ts`, exact-case.\r\n  Include every matching file. When registered, emit `test:setup` and run it from `test`. When no\r\n  file matches, emit neither the project nor the script.\r\n\r\n`conformance`, `integration`, `distribution`, and `service` are separate subjects, not names for\r\none.\r\nKeep `conformance` in `test`: measure this package against an installed official artifact, and start\r\nany server the proof drives itself. Keep `integration` in `test`: compose the workspace's public\r\nsurfaces without packing, installing, or driving an external service. In a publishing workspace,\r\nrun `distribution` and `service` from `prepublishOnly`: pack and install the package in\r\n`distribution`, and drive the real service with `tests/setupService.ts`, longer timeouts, and no file\r\nparallelism in `service`. In a `private: true` workspace, never declare `prepublishOnly`; omit\r\n`distribution`, reach `service` from `test`, and retain the service project's isolated\r\nconfiguration.\r\n\r\nOne project sits on neither axis. `probe` includes `tmp/probe/**/*.test.ts` so an agent can run a\r\nthrowaway instrument against real sources, aliases and setup. Declare no proof there. Keep the\r\nproject composed in the root configuration rather than declared as a path string. The `probe` MCP\r\nserver arms through it — its arming specifications live under the `tmp/probe/` directory and infer\r\nthis project — so a workspace that removes the project, or declares it as a path string, fails the\r\nserver's arming, and an unarmed server refuses every `prove` call. The `test:bench` script runs the\r\nsame project in benchmark mode, which collects every test file under the `tmp/probe/` directory and\r\nthe `tests/` tree while refusing every ordinary test case. Every test script names its project and\r\nthe `test:bench` script joins no chain, so no gate runs either mode; the project's directory is\r\nignored by git; and `.claude/rules/tests.md` governs what may live there.\r\n\r\n- Define a cross-cutting project only for a proof the package actually has.\r\n- Prepare the external service before invoking the `service` project. Use `tests/setupService.ts`\r\n  to verify readiness, apply `.claude/rules/tests.md`, and name the project `service` whatever it\r\n  drives.\r\n- In a publishing workspace, a project leaves the default run when it drives a live external\r\n  service or is hermetic but slow — it spawns processes, packs, installs, or drives a real build.\r\n- Give every isolated project its own script, and place that script by the preceding paragraph.\r\n\r\nSetup assets:\r\n\r\n- `tests/setup.css` declares cascade-layer order before `@import 'tailwindcss'` and its `@source`.\r\n- Browser setup wires `setup.css`.\r\n- Styles setup loads `setup.css` and the compiled cascade.\r\n\r\nScope with `test:src`, `test:src:core`, `test:app`, `test:app:server`, and equivalent scripts. Each\r\ncross-cutting project has its own script too: `test:policy`, `test:config`, `test:setup`, `test:guides`,\r\n`test:conformance`, `test:distribution`, `test:integration`, `test:service`.\r\n\r\n## Typechecking and environment isolation\r\n\r\n`npm run check` is the comprehensive contract. It typechecks the whole tree and\r\nthen runs the configured scoped checks that prove environment isolation.\r\n\r\n- Use plain `tsc` for a TypeScript-only tree.\r\n- Use `vue-tsc` only for a scope containing `.vue` internals.\r\n- `check:src` mirrors configured `src:*` test projects; optional `src:bin` is its\r\n  own scope.\r\n- `check:app` mirrors configured `app:*` projects.\r\n- During development, run the narrowest granular scope that covers the change.\r\n- Lint is a separate complementary gate; neither lint nor root checking replaces\r\n  environment-isolation checks.\r\n\r\n| Scope                        | `lib`                             | `types`           | Permitted host globals                                                                                                                   |\r\n| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\r\n| `src:core`, `app:core`       | `[\"ESNext\",\"WebWorker\"]`          | `[]`              | WHATWG web interop: fetch family, streams, URL, Abort, encoders, crypto, timers, console, DOMException, structuredClone; Separate verified fact from inference.\r\n- Read authoritative types and named decision-bearing implementation files first-hand. Delegate bulk supporting context, never the owning design decision.\r\n- Treat existing code, tests, `old/`, branches, and copied projects as evidence, not authority.\r\n- Build a capability/defect matrix before a broad API or production-readiness change. Every row ends as implement, repair, retain, or intentionally exclude with evidence.\r\n- Fix that matrix when the change starts. It is the definition of done, and the change closes when every row closes.\r\n- Never end a row as \"hardened further.\" Replace any evaluative phrase with the concrete condition that closes the row.\r\n- Record a finding outside the matrix against the row that owns it, for the next matrix. Do not reopen this one.\r\n\r\n## Probes before arguments\r\n\r\nA question a probe can settle is settled by the probe, whether or not anyone has disputed it. Reasoning decides what to run and what the result means. It does not replace the run.\r\n\r\n- Test your own assumptions before you rely on them. You do not need a disagreement to justify a probe. If you are about to depend on what a function returns, what a config resolves to, what a flag does, or whether a path is even reached, run it and find out.\r\n- Treat a long deliberation about behaviour as the signal to stop and run something. Deliberation that a ten-line probe would have ended is the most expensive habit in this process, and it is invisible because it feels like rigour.\r\n- Verify a belief before stating it, or label it as unverified. An unverified assertion put into context becomes a fact for everything downstream, including other agents, and correcting it later costs more than the check would have.\r\n- Hold a claim you issue to the standard you hold a claim you receive. Nothing downstream re-checks an instruction, so an unverified fact inside one becomes the premise of every task built on it. Auditing every report you receive while exempting every brief you write is the common form of this failure.\r\n- Prefer the check over the chain of reasoning whenever the check is cheap. Reading the installed declaration, running one line, or counting the call sites beats three paragraphs inferring the same thing, and it produces evidence you can hand to someone else.\r\n- Write the probe before the argument gets long. The moment a claim about behaviour is disputed — between engines, between a report and a rule, or in your own head — stop and run it. Get the smallest real input through the real code and read the real output.\r\n- Bound the search before starting it, and put the bound in the brief. Name the benchmark, the population, or the row that ends it. An investigation with no stated stopping condition runs until attention runs out. This includes the case where the honest answer is that the limit is inherent and belongs in documentation rather than in code.\r\n- Treat a negative probe as evidence about the probe until its input is shown to reach the code under test. A pass proves nothing if the vector never arrived. Instrument the path, assert an observable side effect, or drive it through a door you can see.\r\n- When a report names a defect and your reproduction comes back clean, assume first that your vector was weaker than theirs, and go get their exact vector. Treating a failed reproduction as a disproof is the most common way a true finding is lost.\r\n- A reported vector the compiler rejects refutes the VECTOR, never the finding. Where a claim asserts reachability through a typed API, compile the exact vector under the project's own settings; re-derive one the types admit before dropping the finding, and record which vector was actually tested.\r\n- Reproduce a reported defect's cause before instructing a fix from it. A real symptom can carry a wrong diagnosis, and a fix aimed at the stated cause edits the wrong file while the defect survives.\r\n- Do not read a result into a tool's failure to find your probe. \"No tests found\", an empty match, a skipped file, a runner that resolved nothing — these report on the harness, not the subject. Confirm the probe was collected and executed first.\r\n- Prefer an observation over a derivation, including your own. When a measurement and an argument disagree, the argument is wrong until the measurement is shown to be broken.\r\n- Diagnose from the artifact the work produces — the file, the count, the exit code, the timestamp on what changed — never from a wrapper or a proxy signal that merely correlates with progress. Read a gate bare: a pipeline stage after it (`| tail`, `| grep`) reports the stage's exit status and hides the gate's failing lines.\r\n- Verify a comment or an agent's report against the call sites before relying on it. A code comment is not evidence. When lanes disagree about whether a path is live, count the callers rather than weighing the prose.\r\n- What a round proves is what it ran. A conclusion carried from one door to another is a hypothesis at the second door. Re-run it there.\r\n\r\n## Falsification\r\n\r\nA review that reads a diff finds what the diff shows. A review that tries to break named claims finds what the diff hides. Code that has passed diff review several times can still carry a defect nobody has tried to trigger.\r\n\r\n### Writing the claims\r\n\r\n- State the subject as a numbered list of the claims the work makes, never as \"review this diff.\" Each claim is falsifiable: a property some concrete input, state, or interleaving could show false.\r\n- Instruct the auditor to attempt refutation, not confirmation. A claim it cannot break is CONFIRMED with the evidence that convinced it. A claim it breaks is BROKEN with the exact failing input, state, or interleaving, plus the smallest correct fix.\r\n- Derive claims from what the change asserts under adverse conditions: cancellation, restart, concurrency, partial failure, hostile input, resource exhaustion, and the orderings a happy path never reaches.\r\n- Read the installed declaration or implementation of every substrate a claim depends on. A claim about `stop()` is unfalsifiable until you know what `stop()` does when the status is not the one the caller assumed.\r\n\r\n### Instruments\r\n\r\n- An instrument is not evidence until it has failed. Pair every probe, comparison, or matrix with a negative control that must report failure, run under the same conditions. An identity check whose control reports \"same\" has measured nothing.\r\n- When a question about a TypeScript edit can supply a workspace project, a case of workspace files with a test, and a negative control naming its files, its test, the stage it must fail at, and why, call the `prove` tool the `probe` MCP server registers before relying on the answer. When the question supplies no project, no case, or no control, follow `.claude/rules/tests.md` § Probes and report the fallback instrument's own control and coverage.\r\n- When no `probe` server is registered in the session, register one outside the repository, in the harness's own local or user MCP scope — in Claude Code, `claude mcp add` outside project scope — naming the installed `node_modules/@orkestrel/probe/dist/bin/main.js` entry, and start it in the repository whose projects the question names, because the server fixes its workspace from its own working directory. The registration cannot live in the tree: a scaffold target holds no `.mcp.json` file, that path is instruction canon, and a copy at it reports as foreign drift on every `scaffold audit` run. Where the harness registers no server at all, treat the question as supplying no project and take the preceding rule's fallback.\r\n- Quote the closing line of the `prove` answer verbatim in every report, brief, and audit verdict that rests on the claim: the `receipt probe:<digest>:…` line when the case ran clean and the control broke exactly where the claim declared it would, and the `no receipt` line otherwise. A `no receipt` line leaves the claim unproved — report it with the stage that refused.\r\n- Read a receipt as evidence about its claim, never as a gate result. The gate chain still runs, and `verifier` still owns its result.\r\n- Draw the negative control from outside the population the instrument covers. Name the instrument's membership rule first, then pick a control that rule excludes. A control sampled from constructs the instrument already handles proves only that it discriminates among those constructs, and says nothing about the class it silently cannot reach.\r\n- State an instrument's coverage beside its result. A conclusion inherits the instrument's scope, not the question's. An unstated coverage claim is read as complete, and it never is. A search proves something about the paths it walked, so name them.\r\n- Match the instrument to the question. A text search reports on text, so a claim about declarations, call sites, or structure needs the compiler or a parser instead. A pattern written for one spelling of a construct reports on that spelling alone. A path check answers relative to the directory it runs from, so resolve the inputs against their own base before reading a miss as a finding.\r\n- Name the rival reading the instrument must exclude, and show it reports differently under that reading. Give independent measurements independent state: one counter shared across members reports read order and per-member read count identically, so a result consistent with both measured neither.\r\n- Report a question unanswered rather than answering it with a weaker instrument. A fallback that measures something adjacent returns a confident wrong answer, and nothing downstream can tell that answer from the real one — searching commit messages for a release when the question is where a version changed will match some release, but not the one asked about. Name the substitute and what it actually measures, or say the question is open.\r\n- State what the controls established and what they did not. An instrument certified only from the inside is trusted exactly where it has never been tested.\r\n- Treat a gap between what an instrument says it checks and what it actually matches as a defect in the instrument, not as a documented limit. A recorded blind spot buys trust only when everything outside it is genuinely covered.\r\n- Measure the product, not the harness. A recorded baseline that counts something about its own fixture is not evidence about the shipped surface, however often a guide quotes it.\r\n- Baseline a published-artifact claim against the published artifact. \"Did my change move the surface\" and \"does this release differ from the last one\" are different questions, and a diff against your own starting point answers only the first. A toolchain that re-emits declarations moves the artifact without any source edit, so every writer can correctly report an unmoved surface while the package's published contract has changed. Fetch what consumers actually have — the tarball, the deployed asset — and compare against that.\r\n- Prove a module cycle by loading the built artifact, not by a green suite. Tests import through the source graph and a bundler resolves it differently, so a cycle that is fatal at module-init in the shipped form can stay invisible under every test. Import each published entry point and read an export from it.\r\n- Adopt an instrument that settled a claim as a test before accepting the work it settled. The probe that proved a fix, carrying the control that proved the probe, is that fix's regression guard. A verification that runs once is a rehearsal, not a gate.\r\n\r\n### Rounds and verdicts\r\n\r\n- Treat an all-confirmed round as a legitimate result, and put the brief on trial rather than the subject. Re-read the claims and ask whether any could have been falsified by evidence the round actually had. If none could, the claims were descriptive and the round proved nothing — sharpen them and re-run. If they could have been and were not, the pass stands.\r\n- Name the claims you could not break either way, so the next round knows what has already been attacked.\r\n- Never tell an auditor that a clean round means it did not try. That instructs it to manufacture a finding, and a manufactured finding costs a fix unit, an argument, and the credibility of the true findings beside it.\r\n- Treat a repaired claim as a new claim, not a settled one. Re-ask it at every entry point that reaches the same rule, not only the door the defect arrived through. The engine that wrote the fix is least able to see this, because re-verifying where the fix is feels like verifying the fix.\r\n- A fix that adopts the auditor's prescription verbatim may close with a mutation probe in place of a fresh audit round: disable the load-bearing line, watch the adopted pin fail, restore it, and commit the pin as the regression guard. A fix that departs from the prescription gets the cross-engine round.\r\n- Let reachability bound the fix. A defect reachable through the package's own shipped code or a documented extension seam falsifies its claim and is repaired now.\r\n- Document the obligation instead when a defect is reachable only through a hypothetical foreign implementation of a contract this package publishes. State it on the interface that owns it and prove the documentation. Do not build coordination machinery against a requirement nobody wrote down. Attacks are unlimited; reachable ones are not, and only the reachable set is a work list.\r\n- **Three rounds at one seam is the budget, and reaching it switches the search strategy rather than stopping the work.** Repeated rounds against one seam are evidence about the design, not evidence of diligence. At the third round, name what the audit is trying to accomplish, then pick the successor strategy from what the recurrence shows.\r\n- Recurrence with a direction — each fix relocates the class along one stream, or the evidence points up a dependency chain — ends the depth search. Run one breadth round that probes the stream's stations in parallel to locate the source, in the shape `.agents/orchestration.md` § Context and decomposition prescribes, then plan the downstream work from the source and size it by the sweep's map.\r\n- Recurrence with no direction makes the seam itself the question. The next unit is a ruling — on the threat model, the mechanism, or the boundary — taken with the same adversarial pass a design gets, not a fourth repair.\r\n- A subject that reprices itself on every edit — a count, a census, a total over prose — has no closing condition and is not a seam. Drop the claim, or recast it as the property the tally stood in for.\r\n- Write the round count down in the capability/defect matrix row that owns the seam, when the seam opens, so it is a fact rather than a feeling. A seam that has consumed more rounds than the rest of the matrix combined has already answered the question.\r\n- State the ruling that ends a seam as the invariant the code will obey, the constraint bounding it against over-correction, and the interface where a consumer meets the obligation. A ruling that names only the defect it replaces produces the opposite defect next round.\r\n- Give every behavioural audit the means to run its attacks. An auditor that cannot execute cannot falsify a behavioural claim: it returns derivations, and a derivation reads exactly like a verdict while being a different thing — it will confirm a claim one probe would break. Treat a report with no executed evidence as a review of the source, and label it as such.\r\n\r\n## Ecosystem reuse\r\n\r\nThe root laws on inspecting declared `@orkestrel/*` capabilities, reusing a matching primitive, and updating every consumer without shims bind here without restatement. This file adds the judgment calls:\r\n\r\n- Prove the semantic difference before keeping a local variant. Similar names are not evidence of different behavior.\r\n- Treat downstream friction as valid evidence of a reusable upstream defect, not as automatic proof. Fix the lowest package that owns the general mechanism and keep product policy downstream.\r\n- Never re-export a dependency's symbol to soften a consumer's import.\r\n\r\n## Production hardening\r\n\r\n- Translate \"enterprise-grade\" or \"production-ready\" into an explicit risk and seam matrix covering applicable inputs, states, failures, cleanup, cancellation, concurrency, resource ownership, hostile boundaries, environment isolation, serialization and restore, and package consumption.\r\n- Grade that matrix on coverage, not optimization: whether every applicable seam exists, works, and stays proven. Do not grade on how many further interleavings can be invented against the one seam already proven. A surface polished past its row buys less than the next uncovered seam would have.\r\n- Test observable invariants at each applicable seam with real implementations.\r\n- Use dedicated real-service projects for external model or service behavior. Require readiness and tune each request to the smallest proof that still exercises the claim.\r\n- Audit test discovery, counts, skipped and todo tests, cleanup, and assertion adequacy. Passing discovered tests alone is insufficient.\r\n- Inspect public exports, declarations, supported runtime targets, and generated outputs.\r\n- Treat a claim that a surface works with an external client as unproven until one representative real client of that class has driven it end to end. With `think: true` a thinking model's\r\n *   daemon separates reasoning natively — returning it on the distinct `message.thinking`\r\n *   channel (read here through `extractThinking`) instead of inline in `message.content`. Either\r\n *   way the per-call {@link ThinkSplitterInterface} is the defensive guarantee: a daemon\r\n *   may ignore `think: false` for a thinking model and inline `<think>` tags, so every\r\n *   content delta routes through the splitter, only clean content is yielded / assembled,\r\n *   and the separated reasoning (plus any daemon-side `message.thinking` deltas) lands on\r\n *   `ProviderResult.thinking`, never in the conversation.\r\n * - **Boundary narrowing.** Every wire value arrives as `unknown` and is\r\n *   narrowed through guards (`isRecord` / `isString` / `isNumber`) — never `as`. A\r\n *   missing / malformed field degrades to a sensible default (empty content, no\r\n *   usage, `{}` arguments), never a throw.\r\n * - **Bounded.** Each call arms a {@link Timeout} for `OllamaOptions.timeout` and\r\n *   passes `AbortSignal.any([timeout.signal, signal])` to `fetch`, so the caller's\r\n *   signal and the deadline both cancel the request. The timeout is always cleared —\r\n *   in `#fetch` if the request fails/aborts, otherwise in the consuming call's `finally`.\r\n * - **Abort recovers partial.** A `stream` cancelled mid-flight throws a\r\n *   `ProviderAbortError` carrying the partial result assembled so far; pairing the\r\n *   `TextDecoder({ stream: true })` with the `createNDJSONParser` parser keeps multi-byte\r\n *   UTF-8 splits and partial lines honest.\r\n * - **Event-free.** A pure functional boundary — no Emitter, no events.\r\n * - **Transport seam.** {@link OllamaOptions.fetch} swaps the transport (default\r\n *   `globalThis.fetch`) and {@link OllamaOptions.headers} is a per-request, possibly\r\n *   async header injector merged over the base `Content-Type` — so a browser runtime\r\n *   can route through the developer's own server with an obfuscated bearer token,\r\n *   without this library ever handling a real API key. Both omitted ⇒ the global `fetch`\r\n *   and only a JSON content type.\r\n *   Orthogonal to the deadline: the hook is awaited inside `#fetch`'s try, so a hook\r\n *   rejection clears the armed timer like any other request failure.\r\n *\r\n * @example\r\n * ```ts\r\n * const provider = new OllamaProvider({ model: 'qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M' })\r\n * const result = await provider.generate(messages, abort.signal)\r\n * ```\r\n */\r\nexport class OllamaProvider implements ProviderInterface {\r\n\treadonly name = 'ollama'\r\n\treadonly #id: string\r\n\treadonly #model: string\r\n\treadonly #url: string\r\n\treadonly #keepAlive: string | number\r\n\treadonly #timeout: number\r\n\treadonly #think: boolean\r\n\treadonly #options: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> | undefined\r\n\treadonly #transport: typeof globalThis.fetch\r\n\treadonly #headers:\r\n\t\t| (() => Readonly<Record<string, string>> | Promise<Readonly<Record<string, string>>>)\r\n\t\t| undefined\r\n\treadonly #format: ContextFormat | undefined\r\n\r\n\tconstructor(options: OllamaOptions) {\r\n\t\tthis.#id = crypto.randomUUID()\r\n\t\tthis.#model = options.model\r\n\t\tthis.#url = options.url ??
